strategy_title: Autotune Tile Sizes for Strided Layout Transpose Kernels
strategy_description: When a Triton pointwise kernel performs a layout transpose (e.g., NCHW→NHWC) with strided stores, hardcoded tile sizes can cause uncoalesced global stores (23% excess sectors) and high L1TEX stall rates (53% of cycles). Adding @triton.autotune with a range of XBLOCK and YBLOCK configs allows the runtime to select the tile shape that best matches the store stride pattern, reducing executed instructions by ~45% and warp cycles per issued instruction from 31.4 to 24.9. Register pressure also dropped from 26 to 16 registers/thread as a side effect of the autotuner selecting a simpler config, further relaxing occupancy limits.
applicable_when: Triton pointwise kernel performs a layout transpose or strided scatter store; kernel has hardcoded XBLOCK/YBLOCK; UncoalescedGlobalAccess rule fires with >15% excess sectors; CPIStall attributes >40% of cycles to L1TEX stalls; kernel has low compute throughput (<20%) with moderate memory throughput
do_not_apply_when: Kernel is already autotuned; grid size is large enough to saturate the device (waves_per_sm >> 1); the store pattern is inherently non-coalescing regardless of tile shape (e.g., fully random scatter); autotuning overhead is unacceptable (e.g., very short-lived kernels called once)
framework_notes: Triton-specific: use @triton.autotune with key=['ynumel','xnumel'] to cache configs per shape. The lambda grid `lambda META: (cdiv(N, META['XBLOCK']), cdiv(M, META['YBLOCK']))` is required when tile sizes are autotuned. In CUDA, the equivalent is launch bound tuning or template parameter sweeps. Register count dropped from 26→16 as a side effect of the autotuner selecting a config with less spill/pressure.
